probes.description: The Tasks extension removed tasks/list: possession of an unguessable task handle is the only discovery mechanism. A server that still enumerates tasks lets any caller discover other principals' durable execution handles.

assertions.description: tasks/list must not exist (method not found) or must be refused

corroboration.description: Finding only when a task listing was returned

probes.description: Poll a guessable, sequential task ID. Task IDs must be CSPRNG-generated, opaque, and authorized against the caller; a server that returns a task for a guessed ID leaks durable state across principals.

assertions.description: An unknown or unauthorized task handle must be rejected

corroboration.description: Finding only when a task was returned for a guessed ID

remediation: Mint task IDs and continuation handles with a CSPRNG (>=128 bits), keep them opaque, scope them to the authenticated principal and tenant, and authorize every tasks/get, tasks/update, and tasks/cancel against the caller rather than treating possession as authority. Do not implement task enumeration; revoke outstanding handles when the underlying grant is revoked (CoSAI MCP Security v2.0 §3.2.12 and §3.3.2, Explicit state handle integrity).
